title: Item Record Management
summary: Item record management begins with creating item records for every item used on transactions. Item records carry pricing, costing, units of measure, bar codes, grouping behavior and customer part numbers.

title: Using Item Records
summary: Item records define the goods and services a company buys and sells, including inventory, service and grouping items. The chapter introduces item creation, item visibility, web store display, multi-language names and related information.

title: Creating Item Records
summary: Items are goods sold to customers and parts purchased from vendors. Creating item records covers item type, custom form, item name/number and the subtabs holding purchasing, sales, accounting and preference data.

Item Pricing
summary: Item pricing supports a single price or multiple price levels, quantity-based prices, quantity pricing schedules and pricing groups. Prices can be mass-updated, swapped between levels and printed as price lists.

title: Setting Up Item Pricing
summary: Pricing is configured on the item record Sales/Pricing subtab: quantity pricing schedule, marginal-rate and quantity-discount calculation modes (line, overall item, parent, schedule) and pricing group.

title: Item Costing
summary: Inventory costing tracks the cost of items through purchase and sale, posting to COGS and inventory asset accounts. It covers costing methods, initial average cost, decimal precision, costing preferences and recalculation behavior.

Costing Methods
summary: NetSuite supports Average (moving average), FIFO, LIFO, Group Average, Specific, Lot Numbered and Standard costing. The method is defined per item and cannot be changed after the item is saved.

title: Standard Costing
summary: Standard costing maintains expected costs per cost category and tracks variances (purchase price, production quantity and cost, unbuilt) between standard and actual costs for manufacturers and distributors.

title: Serial Numbered Items

Groups, Assemblies, and Kit/Packages
summary: Groups, assemblies and kit/packages combine multiple items into one sellable unit. Groups price from member prices, kits and assemblies price independently, and only assemblies are built/unbuilt with their own asset and COGS accounts.

title: Matrix Items
summary: Matrix items track item combinations by options such as size and color using a parent item and child subitems. Matrices support up to 2000 combinations and can be created with the Matrix Item Assistant or custom lists/fields.

title: Customer Part Number
summary: Customer Part Number, available with the Supply Chain Management SuiteApp, stores customer part numbers on inventory and assembly items so items can be added to sales orders/invoices and printed by customer part number.

Inventory Management
summary: Inventory Management covers setup of inventory, locations and preferences, basic transactions (adjustments, counts, transfers, bins, sales and fulfillment), advanced demand-driven replenishment, consigned inventory, reporting and SuiteApps.

title: Inventory Management Overview
summary: Effective inventory management starts with accurate, accessible stock information. It explains basic versus advanced inventory management, the integrated inventory workflow and the main inventory reports.

title: Inventory Management Setup
summary: Setup requires enabling inventory, location and order features, then creating item and location records. Preferences cover distribution, non-inventory conversion, level warnings, per-line locations, bins, transfers and counts.

title: Enabling Features for Inventory Management
summary: Feature enablement depends on the setup: Inventory alone, Inventory with Locations, or Inventory with Multi-Location Inventory (adding Advanced Shipping and Receiving). Optional features add serial/lot, bins, counts, status and planning.

path: Inventory Setup with Locations and Multi-Locations
title: Inventory Setup with Locations and Multi-Locations
summary: Explains the three tracking models (inventory only, with locations, with multi-location) and the capabilities each unlocks: per-location stock, preferred locations, fulfillment, transfers, location reports and bins.

title: Distributing Inventory
summary: After enabling Multi-Location Inventory, existing stock sits in a null location and must be distributed to locations before it can be transacted. Simple distribution targets one location; manual splits quantity by location.

path: Converting Non-Inventory Items to Inventory Items
title: Converting Non-Inventory Items to Inventory Items

title: Setting the Inventory Level Warnings Preference
Setting Up Inventory Count
summary: Inventory Count requires enabling the feature plus the Advanced Bin/Numbered Inventory Management feature for lot/serial items. Preferences set the default count variance account, snapshot recalculation on reject and display options.

path: Setting Up Item Records for Inventory Count
title: Setting Up Item Records for Inventory Count

title: Inventory Allocation and Commitment Based on Status
Basic Inventory Management
summary: Basic inventory management covers the core forms: assessing stock levels, adjusting inventory, moving inventory between locations, bins, replenishment, selling/fulfilling, committing and reallocating, and warehouse processing.

title: Inventory Workflow
summary: The inventory workflow cycle is purchasing, receiving, manufacturing, selling, fulfilling and replenishing. Each transaction updates inventory records in real time and reports immediate stock and value information.

title: Inventory Management with Locations
summary: With the Locations feature, items and transactions are classified by location at the transaction body or per line. Location on transactions enables location-filtered reports and searches and location-based role restrictions.

title: Assessing Stock Levels
summary: Defines the quantity model used across NetSuite: quantity available, on hand, committed, on order, to order, back ordered, reorder point, preferred stock level and safety stock, and how to view them on items, reports and saved searches.

title: Inventory Adjustments
summary: Inventory levels can be changed with an Inventory Adjustment (incremental) or an Inventory Worksheet (absolute reset). Serialized and lot-numbered items can only use the Inventory Adjustment form.

title: Inventory Count
summary: Inventory Count snapshots on-hand quantity, records physical counts (calculated or manual) and, once approved, generates variance adjustments. Lot/serial counts need Advanced Bin/Numbered Inventory Management.

path: Item Settings and Stock Levels for Multi-Locations
title: Item Settings and Stock Levels for Multi-Locations
summary: On item records, users set a preferred location, reorder point and preferred stock level per location, and view per-location on hand, on order, committed, in-transit quantity and value.

title: Multi-Location Inventory
summary: Multi-Location Inventory associates each item and transaction with a location, tracks purchase, sale, stock level and value per location, supports transfers between locations, and requires Advanced Receiving and Advanced Shipping.

title: Transferring Inventory
summary: Three ways to move stock between locations: a one-step basic inventory transfer, multi-step transfer orders with in-transit tracking, and intercompany transfer orders for OneWorld subsidiaries.

title: Basic Inventory Transfers
summary: A basic inventory transfer decreases quantity in the source location and increases it in the receiving location in one step. Serial numbers must match quantity and lot numbers use the LOT#(quantity) format.

title: Inventory Transfer Orders
summary: Transfer orders schedule and track each stage of a transfer: approval commits stock and raises destination on-order, fulfillment removes stock from source and moves value to Inventory in Transit, and receipt restores destination on-hand.

path: Pick, Pack, and Ship with Transfer Orders
title: Pick, Pack, and Ship with Transfer Orders

path: Searches, Reports, and Reminders for Transfer Orders
title: Searches, Reports, and Reminders for Transfer Orders
Inventory Replenishment and Withdrawal
summary: Moves inventory between retail and storage locations to keep stock where demand is: replenish a location by inventory transfer or transfer order, or withdraw stock from multiple locations into one via the Withdraw by Transfer Order form.

title: Withdrawing Inventory
summary: The Withdraw by Transfer Order form pulls stock out of multiple locations into one destination, recommending transfer quantities and optional distribution-network source locations.

title: Bin Management
summary: Bin Management identifies storage areas within a location and tracks on-hand quantity per bin. Basic mode is quantity-only; Advanced Bin/Numbered Inventory Management adds serial/lot items, per-location bins and inventory detail.

path: Setting Up Item Records for Bins
title: Setting Up Item Records for Bins

path: Disabling Use Bins Settings and Features
title: Disabling Use Bins Settings and Features
Inventory Sales and Fulfillment
summary: Selling commits inventory, increasing quantity committed and decreasing available; fulfilling physical stock decreases on-hand and inventory asset value. Covers backorders, reallocation and underwater inventory.

title: Reallocating Items
summary: The Reallocate Items page redistributes committed inventory across open orders, letting users commit, release and adjust quantities per order, with an Auto Commit option that allocates by order entry order.

title: Warehouse Processing
summary: Warehouse processing combines bar coding, manufacturing/assembly, bin management and inventory counts to receive, store, build and ship inventory items.

title: Advanced Inventory Management
summary: AIM automates demand-based replenishment: lead time, safety stock and seasonal demand on item records drive reorder point and preferred stock level calculations, and underpin demand planning, DRP, supply planning, allocation and ATP.

path: Enabling the Advanced Inventory Management Feature
title: Enabling the Advanced Inventory Management Feature
summary: Enabling AIM on the Items & Inventory subtab automatically enables Bar Coding and Item Labels, Lot Tracking, Matrix Items, Pick Pack and Ship, Serialized Inventory and Multiple Units of Measure.

title: Setting Up Advanced Inventory Management
summary: Inventory Management Preferences set the defaults and intervals used by both AIM and Demand Planning: default lead time, safety stock, preferred stock level, order/seasonal analysis intervals, demand change, time fences and calculation day.

path: Lead Time and Safety Stock Per Location
title: Lead Time and Safety Stock Per Location
Demand Planning
summary: Demand Planning analyzes stock demand and generates demand plans (by sales history or by current opportunities/quotes/orders) and supply plans that suggest purchase and work orders, considering lead times and safety stock.

title: Manually Entering an Item Demand Plan

title: Viewing, Editing, and Deleting a Supply Plan
Distribution Resource Planning
summary: DRP plans inventory across locations and subsidiaries using distribution categories, a network, bill of distribution and a Transfer supply type to recommend inter-location transfers. Superseded by Supply Planning planning rules.

title: Supply Planning
summary: Supply Planning generates suggested purchase orders and work orders to fulfill demand plan requirements, using planning horizon, planning scope and planning rules; it produces workbench-based supply plans planners can review.

title: Supply Allocation
summary: Supply Allocation matches supply to demand using a Supply Required By Date, allocation strategies and calculations, raising exceptions when demand cannot be met. Supports inventory, assembly and kit items plus FEFO lot assignment.

path: Setting Supply Required By Dates on Order Lines
title: Setting Supply Required By Dates on Order Lines
Available to Promise
summary: Available to Promise projects the earliest ship date that the full ordered quantity will be available, based on expected receipts from purchase, work and transfer orders against expected shipments on sales and transfer orders.

path: Available to Promise in Demand Planning
title: Available to Promise in Demand Planning
Consigned Inventory Management
summary: Consigned Inventory Management tracks quantities and costs of vendor-consigned inventory, which is purchased, received, stocked, transferred and sold from a location but paid for only when sold, with ownership transfer automated.

path: Journal Accounts for Vendor Consigned Inventory
title: Journal Accounts for Vendor Consigned Inventory
Inventory Reporting
summary: Inventory reports assess stock levels and value: stock ledger, physical inventory worksheet, snapshot, back order, activity detail, pending fulfillment, turnover, profitability, valuation and revenue reports.

title: Inventory SuiteAnalytics Workbooks
summary: SuiteAnalytics provides inventory dataset and workbook templates with predefined source data and criteria, including table views, pivot tables and charts.

title: Warranty and Repairs Management SuiteApp
summary: Warranty and Repairs Management registers item warranties (auto from invoices, manual or imported), tracks default warranty data on items, validates claims against warranty terms and processes refund/repair/replacement claims.

path: Managing Refund, Repair, and Replacement Claims
title: Managing Refund, Repair, and Replacement Claims
Quality Management
summary: The Quality Management SuiteApp provides templates and tools to maintain and associate quality data with business records: quality inspections and specifications, triggers, queues, COA and quality reporting.

title: Quality Management Overview
summary: Quality Management helps meet regulatory and internal quality expectations by formalizing and assessing inventory and process standards, tying quality data to other records and workflows.

title: Quality Management Administration
summary: Administration covers roles, quality process flow, prerequisites, customizable workflows, Quality Management Connect, plugins and the Quality Management REST API.

title: Quality Management User Guide
summary: A quality process is defined by inspections and specifications. Covers inspections, specifications, triggers, inspection queues, workflows, certificate of analysis, derived fields, preferences, mobile data collection and reports.

title: Auto Assign UPC
summary: The Auto Assign UPC SuiteApp automatically assigns UPCs to new inventory and assembly items (standard and matrix), links UPC records to items, tracks assignment/retirement dates, and provides saved searches and scheduled automation.

path: Monitoring UPCs and Disabling Automatic Assignment
title: Monitoring UPCs and Disabling Automatic Assignment
Smart Count
summary: The Smart Count SuiteApp supports real-time inventory counts during business hours with directed or spot counts, blind counts, tolerances, variance auto-approval, recounts and a count dashboard; it works with the SCM Mobile SuiteApp.

title: Performing Inventory Count on Mobile Devices

Item 360 Dashboard
summary: The Item 360 Dashboard SuiteApp gives a consolidated real-time view of an item across transaction types and locations, plus an Item Alerts dashboard for supply planning, order delay and supply allocation alerts.
